newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Top U.N. official in Cambodia to discuss concerns.
newsitem.headline: Top U.N. official in Cambodia to discuss concerns.

text.p: A top U.N. official flew into Cambodia on Friday to discuss the country's political turmoil following a recent deadly grenade attack and a widening rift in the coalition government.
"These events have led to an increase in concern," U.N. Assistant Secretary General for Political Affairs Alvaro De Soto told reporters at the start of his 24-hour visit.
He was referring to a March 30 grenade attack on an opposition rally in Phnom Penh that killed up to 19 people.

Following the attack, tension rose dramatically between the royalist FUNCINPEC party and the formerly communist Cambodian People's Party (CPP), which formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run elections in 1993.

"The Secretary General (Kofi Annan) asked me to stop by...in order to talk to the leaders and get a reading of the situation," said De Soto. He was scheduled to meet feuding co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh (FUNCINPEC) and Hun Sen (CPP) later on Friday.
"It's preliminary concern. We still don't have a final assessment of the situation," the U.N. official stressed.

The U.N., which had been asked to help Cambodia prepare for local and general elections due before the end of next year, would be worried if the situation were to deteriorate further and affect the conduct of the polls, he said.
The United Nations had "strong hope that matters can be solved without any need for external assistance, but we are standing by."
De Soto, however, ruled out the return of U.N. blue berets to Cambodia.

The U.N. Transitional Authority in Cambodia (UNTAC), made up of more than 20,000 civilians and soldiers from around 30 countries, was sent to Cambodia to oversee a 1991 peace pact between warrring rivals and left after the 1993 elections.
